onset.summary: Argentine hard-currency bonds trade at deeply distressed prices and the government has put a restructuring proposal to creditors while an interest payment sits inside its grace period. Reserves are thin, the economy is contracting into the pandemic, and negotiations with large bondholders are unresolved.

indicators.description: Hard-currency bonds trading at deeply distressed prices
Government has tabled a debt-restructuring proposal to creditors

outcome.summary: The grace period on a bond coupon payment lapsed on 22 May 2020 without payment, a sovereign default; a restructuring of the country's foreign-law bonds was agreed with major creditors later in the year.

onset.summary: World trade and commodity prices are contracting sharply and every large advanced economy is shrinking. Australia is a commodity exporter heavily exposed to external demand, its currency and terms of trade have dropped, and forecasters widely expect its output to turn negative for consecutive quarters.

indicators.description: Commodity terms of trade falling steeply from their peak
World merchandise trade volumes contracting quarter on quarter

outcome.summary: Australian output did not record two consecutive quarters of contraction through the evaluation window; a large fiscal stimulus, rate cuts and resilient resource exports kept annual growth positive.

cases.control_rationale: The external demand shock hit Australia hard, but policy support and commodity demand meant the declared downturn outcome did not materialise for the target within the horizon.

onset.summary: The smallest of the US independent investment banks is denying market rumours about its liquidity. It finances a large book of mortgage-related securities overnight in tri-party repo, so its funding must be renewed each morning by lenders who are themselves under redemption pressure, and it has no access to the central-bank discount window.

outcome.summary: Cash ran out within days. The central bank authorised financing against a ring-fenced pool of the firm's assets to facilitate its acquisition by a larger bank, and opened the Primary Dealer Credit Facility to lend to primary dealers.

onset.summary: A large French bank is preparing to suspend subscriptions and redemptions in three funds exposed to US subprime-linked asset-backed securities because liquidity in those segments has evaporated and the assets can no longer be valued. Rating agencies have downgraded swathes of subprime paper, asset-backed commercial paper conduits cannot roll maturing notes, and a German lender has already needed rescue over similar exposures.

outcome.summary: The funds were gated on 9 August 2007, euro overnight rates jumped above the policy rate and the central bank injected emergency liquidity the same morning; term interbank markets never returned to pre-August spreads. onset.summary: A globally systemic Swiss bank's largest shareholder has publicly ruled out putting in more capital, a day after the annual report disclosed material weaknesses in financial-reporting controls. Its credit-default swaps trade at distressed levels and its shares are at a record low; it lost more than 100 billion Swiss francs of client money in the prior quarter, and wealth clients can move balances in a day.

outcome.summary: A large central-bank liquidity line did not stop the outflows, and over the weekend of 19 March 2023 the authorities forced a sale to the other Swiss global bank under emergency law, writing about 16 billion francs of additional tier-1 bonds to zero while shareholders received stock.

onset.summary: A private-banking-focused lender with wealthy coastal clients is losing deposits fast as savers compare it with a bank closed days earlier. Roughly two-thirds of its deposits exceed the insurance cap and its assets are long-dated low-rate jumbo mortgages and municipal bonds worth far less than carrying value; eleven large banks are placing an uninsured deposit with it to steady confidence.

outcome.summary: The private deposit backstop delayed but did not stop the outflow; about 100 billion dollars left in the first quarter, and the bank was closed on 1 May 2023 and sold immediately to the largest US bank, the second-largest US bank collapse on record.

onset.summary: The oldest US money-market fund holds several hundred million dollars of a large broker-dealer's commercial paper whose issuer has just entered court protection. onset.summary: Emergency official purchases have pulled the government-bond market back from the seizure of mid-March, but conditions remain fragile. Bid-offer spreads on long-dated bonds, though well below their peak, are still wider than pre-stress norms, primary dealers' capacity to warehouse inventory is stretched against continued selling by foreign holders and levered funds, and the central bank is the marginal buyer holding the market together. The alert is whether disorderly trading returns once official support is scaled back.

indicators.description: Bid-offer spreads on long-dated government bonds remain above pre-stress norms though off their peak
Primary-dealer balance-sheet capacity to absorb government bonds remains stretched relative to demand
Central-bank large-scale purchases remain the marginal buyer stabilising the market

outcome.summary: No renewed disorderly dysfunction returned to the government-bond market through the evaluation window. After the spring interventions, official measures of the market's capacity to absorb large trades had largely recovered toward pre-pandemic ranges, and the central bank sustained market functioning while slowing its Treasury purchases from the emergency spring pace.

cases.control_rationale: The market had seized in March, but by the observation point official backstops had restored basic functioning; the open question was whether disorderly conditions would recur, and they did not through the horizon, so the declared market-liquidity outcome did not occur for the target.
